questions.prompt: What is the delivery model of Redis Pub/Sub?

options.text: At-least-once, with messages persisted until acknowledged
Fire-and-forget / at-most-once — messages aren't stored
Exactly-once, guaranteed
Ordered and durable, like a log

questions.explanation: Pub/Sub delivers messages only to clients subscribed at publish time and stores nothing — so a subscriber that isn't listening misses the message permanently.

questions.prompt: What does the integer returned by PUBLISH mean?

options.text: The number of clients that received the message
The number of messages stored for later delivery
Confirmation that every subscriber processed the message
The channel's total message count

questions.explanation: PUBLISH returns how many subscribers received the message. It says nothing about whether they successfully processed it.

questions.prompt: Which are true about Pub/Sub? Select all that apply.

options.text: A subscriber that connects later cannot see past messages
PSUBSCRIBE subscribes to channels by glob pattern
Messages are written to disk and can be replayed
On a RESP2 connection in subscribe mode, you can only run (un)subscribe commands

questions.explanation: No history, pattern subscriptions, and the RESP2 subscribed-connection restriction are all true. Pub/Sub does NOT persist or replay messages.

questions.prompt: You must not lose 'process this payment' messages even if the worker briefly restarts. What should you use?

options.text: Pub/Sub with PSUBSCRIBE
Streams with consumer groups and acknowledgements
Pub/Sub on a dedicated connection
Sharded Pub/Sub

questions.explanation: Streams persist entries and support at-least-once delivery via consumer groups and XACK, so a restarting worker can catch up — Pub/Sub would drop messages sent while it was down.

questions.prompt: The Cluster-friendly variant of PUBLISH that keeps a channel on the shard that owns it is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: Sharded Pub/Sub (SPUBLISH/SSUBSCRIBE, added in Redis 7.0) scopes a channel to one shard so publishing scales on Cluster.

questions.prompt: Why is cache invalidation over Pub/Sub often paired with TTLs?

options.text: TTLs make Pub/Sub messages persistent
A server that misses the invalidation message will still drop the stale value when its TTL expires
Pub/Sub requires a TTL to function
TTLs increase PUBLISH throughput

questions.explanation: Because a briefly-disconnected server can miss the invalidation broadcast, a TTL guarantees the stale entry eventually expires anyway — a safety net for the at-most-once delivery.
